title: Question 7
stem:
A student sets up the circuit shown in Fig. 7.1 to measure the charge on a capacitor C for different
values of potential difference across the capacitor.
The variation with potential difference V of the charge Q stored on the capacitor is shown in
Fig. 7.2.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
State and explain how Fig. 7.2 indicates that there is a systematic error in the readings of one
of the meters.

markscheme_points.text: line has non-zero intercept/line does not pass through origin
charge is/should be proportional to potential (difference) or charge is/should be zero when p.d. is zero (therefore there is a systematic error)

hints: Hint 1: Focus on the physical mechanism in A Level Physics theory and principles that causes this behavior.
Hint 2: Rearrange the algebraic equation to isolate the target variable before substituting numerical values.

parts.text:
Use Fig. 7.2 to determine the capacitance, in $\mu\mathrm{F}$, of capacitor C.
$$\text{capacitance} = \text{................................................... }\mu\mathrm{F}$$

markscheme_points.text: reasonable attempt at line of best fit
use of gradient of line of best fit clear

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
Use your answer in (b) to determine the additional energy stored in the capacitor C when the
potential difference across it is increased from $6.0\,\mathrm{V}$ to $9.0\,\mathrm{V}$.
$$\text{energy} = \text{................................................... }\mathrm{J}$$

markscheme_points.text: energy = ½ CV 2 or energy = ½ QV and C = Q / V

hints: Hint 1: Identify all given parameters and units, then recall the fundamental equation in capacitors and dielectric fields connecting them.
Hint 2: Rearrange the algebraic equation to isolate the target variable before substituting numerical values.
Hint 3: Ensure all quantities are expressed in standard SI base units and verify your intermediate arithmetic before writing the final result to 2 or 3 significant figures.
parts.proper_answer: energy = ½ CV 2 or energy = ½ QV and C = Q / V; ∆ energy = ½ × 2800 × 10-6 × (9.02 - 6.02); = 6.3 × 10-2 J
walkthrough:
Step 1: **Identify Governing Principle**

Step 2: **Substitute Values & Calculate**

energy = ½ CV 2 or energy = ½ QV and C = Q / V; ∆ energy = ½ × 2800 × 10-6 × (9.02 - 6.02); = 6.3 × 10-2 J
Verify intermediate arithmetic carefully.

Step 3: **Units & Significant Figures**
